https://carbuzz.com/praga-bohema-spa-lap.text: By Evan Williams Published Aug 20, 2026, 4:25 PM EDT Evan Williams is an automotive journalist and mechanical engineering technologist with more than a decade of experience in the industry. He has written for the Toronto Star and AutoTrader Canada and previously served as editor of Wheelscene.ca . A four-time Canadian Automotive Journalism Award winner, he is the current President of the Automobile Journalists Association of Canada, where he oversees the Canadian Car of the Year Awards program. At CarBuzz for the last year, Evan uses his engineering background to analyze vehicle tech and patents, with a focus on the details that defines great cars. You can unsubscribe anytime. What was meant to be a nice Spa day just turned into a hard day at work for Czech hypercar company Praga. It was only at the Spa-Francorchamps circuit in Belgium for a track day with customers and guests. But with a company test driver behind the wheel, the 700-horsepower Praga Bohema has taken the record at the iconic track. And it's not like this was some obscure record set 30 years ago by a hot hatchback. Praga took the record from a Pagani, and the company did it while other cars were on the track. A Spa Day Became Celebration Instead Of Relaxation Praga Bohema Spa record Praga Praga was at Spa for a track day run by a company called Curbstone events. It puts on track days at some of the biggest circuits in Europe, letting owners experience their cars to full effect. The Bohema was there for "what was intended to be a straightforward customer driving event." It was a standard car on road-legal tires without any special preparation, which is remarkable when automakers can spend months preparing for a Nürburgring record lap and still fail for the smallest of reasons. Company test driver Aleš Jirásek was piloting the Bohema that day. He said that "after a few sessions, we realized the conditions were good and decided to see what the Bohema could do." What it could do was run a 2:21.42 around the longest circuit on the F1 calendar. The time puts it almost two full seconds up on the old record, a 2:23.08 that was set by the driver of a Pagani Huayra BC in 2019. That's a long time for a record to stand, so it shows how quick the Bohema really can be. A Daily Driver Track Beast? Praga Bohema Spa record Praga Praga calls this the lap record for a "type-approved, road-legal car on road-legal tires at Spa-Francorchamps." So a real production road car on tires that could stay on for the drive home. The car comes with Pirelli Trofeo R rubber, which isn't exactly a typical all-season, but it is much more streetable than the available Michelin slicks. With Jirásek having to plan his lap around the other drivers enjoying the circuit, and without even tweaking the suspension for the track, the time is even more impressive. "This achievement perfectly captures what the Bohema is all about," said company owner Tomas Kasparek. "It was never intended to be a compromised track special. Our objective was to combine genuine race-car performance with the freedom and usability of a road-legal supercar." Front three-quarter view of the only Praga Bohema in America. Roger Biermann/CarBuzz/Valnet The Bohema is a sub 2,200-pound hypercar that makes nearly the same weight in downforce at 155 miles per hour. It has 700 horsepower from a version of the 3.8-liter twin-turbo V6 you'd normally find in a Nissan GT-R. British performance experts Litchfield tweaked the carbon fiber car's engine for this application. Praga can add this record to its list, which includes fast times at some other very impressive tracks in Europe. It also set a seriously quick time around the Top Gear test track, where former Stig Ben Collins drove it there and back, and in the middle of his Sunday drive was just 0.1 seconds off the 1,139 hp Aston Martin Valkyrie's best time. CarBuzz Insight – Why This Matters: Generally speaking, automakers setting track records has become a clichéd blob of marketing that has very little relevance in the real world. However, if Praga is being completely honest about this record (and we believe they are), this is actually a very notable achievement because it's not something manufactured, if you will. There was no prep work, no planning, no attempt to spin the narrative for a favorable outcome, regardless of the actual outcome. This was a really fast car demonstrating its capability in a real-world environment. Yes, there was a phenomenal driver behind the wheel, but running street-legal tires while zipping around cars and still taking a record set by a Pagani? That speaks more for the car and the company than any Nürburgring attempt planned out months in advance. Google is updating how content is shown. https://www.azernews.az/culture/262725.h.text: TÜRKSOY marks 20 years of photographers’ meetings with Budapest exhibition [PHOTOS] 23 August 2026 10:00 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more An anniversary exhibition marking the 20th anniversary of the TÜRKSOY Photographers’ Meeting has opened in Budapest, showcasing images highlighting Hungary’s historical, cultural and natural heritage. The exhibition was organised through cooperation between the International Organisation of Turkic Culture (TÜRKSOY) and the Lakitelek Foundation, and was created as part of the 20th edition of the photographers’ meeting. Thirteen photographers from different countries and regions of the Turkic world took part in the initiative. Their works, produced during an 11-day programme, are now on display at the Budapest Art Bridge (BAB) Gallery. During the programme, the photographers travelled to Budapest, Pannonhalma, Kalocsa, Hortobágy and the UNESCO World Heritage village of Hollókő, documenting Hungary’s historic monuments, traditional arts, cultural traditions and natural landscapes. The exhibition also features photographs from the Great Kurultáj, a Hun-Turkic cultural gathering held in Bugac, including images of equestrian performances, traditional costumes and ceremonies. Other highlights include the traditional pastoral life of the Hortobágy plains, Przewalski horses at the Pentezug Wild Horse Reserve, and examples of Kalocsa’s distinctive ceramic art, traditional clothing and decorative wall painting. The TÜRKSOY Photographers’ Meeting has been held for 20 years with the aim of building a rich visual archive of the cities, people, traditions and cultural heritage of the Turkic world. The Budapest exhibition underlines the initiative’s broader role in documenting and promoting the cultural links connecting Turkic communities and regions through photography. https://www.politico.eu/article/canada-m.text: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Sunday that he is not seeking full EU membership but wants to forge much closer ties with the bloc, as he prepares to travel to Strasbourg amid an escalating trade war with the U.S. “We’re not looking to become a member of the European Union,” Carney told reporters at the Toronto International Film Festival. “What we are looking — and will begin discussions for — [is] a unique alliance with the European Union.” “We share the same values, we have the same priorities and we have very complementary strengths,” he added. Advertisement Advertisement Carney will address the European Parliament this week and attend Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s State of the Union speech Wednesday. His comments follow a Wall Street Journal report suggesting that he has floated making Canada an “associate member” of the EU — a novel status rather than an existing category of membership. Officials have discussed closer cooperation on critical minerals, trade, education and cultural exchanges, digital infrastructure and Arctic security. Carney’s European pivot comes after months of increasingly hostile trade relations with Washington. In August, U.S. President Donald Trump imposed 50 percent tariffs on a range of Canadian goods, including cars, alcohol and dairy. That prompted Ottawa to retaliate and eventually suspend trade talks between the two countries, after what Carney called “unfair” last-minute U.S. demands. Trump has also repeatedly needled Ottawa over Canadian sovereignty — from calling the country a potential 51st state to ordering Lake Ontario to be renamed “Lake America” for U.S. federal use. Canada will make its Eurovision debut in 2027 and it will also host an EU summit in Montreal on Oct. 29-30. Brussels, however, has yet to endorse Carney’s “associate member” idea, while parts of the existing EU-Canada trade agreement still await ratification in several member countries.

https://www.politico.eu/article/serbian-.text: BELGRADE — Brussels has lost its man in Belgrade. The opposition Student List’s landslide victory on Sunday ended Aleksandar Vučić’s 12-year run as the EU’s key interlocutor in Serbia. For more than a decade, every step of the candidate country’s accession process and trade negotiations had to pass through him. “Aleksandar Vučić acted like the go-to person for everything while ignoring all the laws in the country, including the constitution,” Jugoslav Gašić, an assistant professor in medicine at several universities and soon-to-be MP, said in an interview. Advertisement Advertisement When POLITICO reached him, Gašić was in the middle of grading student papers — a fitting snapshot of a new parliamentary majority made up largely of professors, doctors and other political novices. The Student List won an outright parliamentary majority at the weekend: a stunning result for a leaderless movement born out of protests. The party’s first order of business will be undoing much the legacy of Vučić and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS), starting with reversing years of rule-of-law rollbacks. But it will also reset Serbia’s relationship with Brussels, which the Student List argues the former leader managed more as a transactional tool than a genuine path to EU membership. “Ultimately, [Vučić] always represented his own interests and not the interests of Serbia,” said Gašić. Representatives for the SNS didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment. Even among Serbia’s most committed pro-Europeans, Brussels’ willingness to route all progress through Vučić personally has left a bitter aftertaste. Advertisement Advertisement “The key lesson that should be drawn from the case of Serbia is that the EU can very easily lose credibility and integrity if it ignores the causes of democratic backsliding in a country,” said Srdjan Majstorović, chairman of the governing board of the European Policy Center (CEP), a think tank. According to CEP data published earlier this year, as many 41.6% of citizens believe the EU is more interested in pursuing its own political and economic interests in the region than improving the state of democracy and the rule of law in the country. For years, anytime non-governmental organizations, journalists or activists argued that Brussels should try to include other voices in the EU negotiation process, they were told “that there was no alternative to the regime in Serbia,” Majstorović continued. Ilija Srdanovic, the first person on the Student’s List, celebrates at the Student’s List headquarters in Belgrade after Aleksandar Vučić conceded the elections. | Andrej Ivanov/Getty Images The Student List’s election program casts the EU as Serbia’s most important economic partner and pledged to deepen Belgrade’s existing strategic partnerships with EU members such as Greece, Italy, Hungary and France, while seeking closer bilateral ties with other European capitals. It does not, however, explicitly name EU membership as an immediate goal. Gašić wouldn’t be drawn on concrete aims for the Serbia-EU relationship, but said: “We don’t want to be cut off by Europe. We don’t want to be an isolated island.” Advertisement Advertisement “I respect how well-ordered they are, the rule of law and democratic principles,” he added. “Yet I think we need to reset our priorities with the EU, where we consider Serbia’s interests first. A one-sided approach doesn’t foster long-term cooperation.” The Student List grew out of a mass protest movement sparked by a 2024 railway station roof collapse that killed 16 people. Students blamed the deaths on corruption in state construction contracts and began blockading universities, and within months the protests had swelled into the largest Serbia had seen in decades. Brussels’ response was muted as students marched across the country, with EU officials largely avoided criticizing Vučić directly. EU flags were conspicuously absent from the demonstrations. The European Commission didn’t respond to a request for comment for this article. “The Commission must first restore its long-lost credibility after years of propping up Vučić,” said Djordje Bojović, a foreign policy advisor for Greens in the European Parliament. He said that Serbia has long been demonized and struggled to reinvent its image since the 1990s, an image “only further cemented by Vučić’s repressive authoritarianism.” Advertisement Advertisement Despite those concerns, Serbia’s economic ties with Europe flourished during Vučić’s time in power, with the country becoming one of the region’s leading destinations for foreign investment. Under Vučić, Serbia went from about €750 million in foreign direct investment in 2012 to more than €30 billion over the following decade, more than the rest of the Western Balkans combined. In Brussels, figures such as Bojović and representatives of the opposition parties would plead with institutions such as the Parliament and the Commission to meet with them or take their concerns seriously. “Vučić had convinced all of them that the opposition is not worth talking to and that they’re not credible,” Bojović said. Now, with SNS firmly relegated to the opposition, Brussels will need to rethink how it works with Serbia. To many Serbians, the EU has 12 years of looking the other way to answer for first.
